newsitem.title: USA: Charlton Heston elected vice president of NRA.
newsitem.headline: Charlton Heston elected vice president of NRA.

text.p: Actor Charlton Heston will add "a big megaphone" for the National Rifle Association (NRA) goal of keeping guns in the hands of "law-abiding gun owners," the group's leader said on Tuesday.

Heston, 72, the actor who played Moses and parted the Red Sea, was elected first vice president on Monday by the 76-member NRA board, defeating incumbent Neal Knox, a hardliner who had led a challenge to oust Wayne LaPierre, the executive vice president and leader of the group.
Heston's narrow victory followed weeks of bitter infighting in the powerful gun lobby group as Knox sought to unseat LaPierre and steer the NRA in a different direction.
LaPierre, who was re-elected along with the group's president Marion Hammer, hailed Heston's victory.

"Charlton Heston adds a big megaphone to the National Rifle Association in terms of its message," LaPierre said on Tuesday, "which is, keep violent criminals off the street and keep your hands off law-abiding gun owners' guns."
Heston's election as first vice president means he is in line to be tapped as president of the NRA next year.

"If Charlton Heston wants to be president of the NRA, I cannot imagine a board of directors not electing Charlton Heston to that position," LaPierre said. "There would be a nationwide revolt among our members ... He's Moses to our people. I'm serious."
Speaking to reporters on Monday, Heston said serving on the NRA board was one of the high points of his career.

Heston, a staunch Republican and a long-time member of the NRA, is widely expected to help repair the NRA's image, which has been tarnished by its opposition to the assault weapons ban and inflammatory comments by top NRA officials.
Heston, who made his theatrical debut as Santa Claus in a school play at age 5, became Hollywood's leading epic hero.
From Moses to Michelangelo, the Oscar-winning actor portrayed real-life luminaries with an integrity made all the more imposing by his muscular physique, rock-jawed face and resonant voice.
He is best known for his role as Moses in the 1956 epic "The 10 Commandments" in which he parted the Red Sea. In addition to playing Moses, Heston did the voice of God.
